text:
emma (Support): hi @customer-ACME — I saw your email, can you paste the request id or an example request?
customer-ACME: thanks — our staging job suddenly burned ~45k credits overnight. we only expected 2k. no code change. request id in logs: req_20250317_9f8c.
emma (Support): ugh, that is big. do you call /v1/embeddings or /v1/rerank?
customer-ACME: embeddings. it's a background worker that embeds rows in batches. we saw a bunch of 502s then retries.
raj (Billing): quick note: embeddings are billed per embedding unit *and* per-call overhead if you're batching poorly. small batches + retries can multiply cost.
mike (SRE): can you share the worker retry config? are you using our SDK with automatic retries or custom logic?
customer-ACME: we use our internal job runner with this snippet:```python
for row in rows:
  try:
    embed = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-xl", input=row.text)
  except Exception as e:
    time.sleep(1)
    embed = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-xl", input=row.text)
```
(mike): lol that explains a lot — serial single-item calls + immediate retry on any error = multiplier. also if the 502 was transient and the job loops, it can spike.
priya (Eng): confirm: embedding billing counts per embedding vector. if you do 10k rows and retry each once, that's ~20k embedding units. plus if you didn't batch, per-call overhead can be higher.
customer-ACME: is there a way to map those billing records back to request ids? we only have the req_... id from our app.
emma (Support): yes we'll correlate. @billing-bot can you pull logs for req_20250317_9f8c and list all embedding calls and billed units?
billing-bot: pulled events for req_20250317_9f8c — 18,432 embedding units billed across 4xx/5xx and 2xx responses, 11,014 calls from that job in a 2h window. breakdown attached (redacted).
raj (Billing): based on the breakdown, most calls were identical inputs repeated due to retry logic; we can offer a partial credit for the repeated failed attempts.
priya (Eng): recommendations: 1) batch inputs (client supports up to 512 inputs per embeddings call), 2) add exponential backoff and idempotency keys, 3) detect transient 5xx and avoid immediate retry with zero delay.
mike (SRE): also add circuit breaker on job: if error rate > 30% for 5m, pause consumer and alert.
customer-ACME: thanks — we'll patch this. can you refund credits now?
raj (Billing): we can credit the duplicated successful attempts and the calls that returned 5xx before retries. I'll issue a one-time 20k-credit refund while we investigate the rest. will also add a note to your account about applying free-trial promo twice?
emma (Support): action items: 1) raj to apply 20k credit (in progress), 2) priya/mike to draft docs snippet on batching + retry patterns, 3) customer to deploy patch with backoff and batching.
priya (Eng): here's a quick example we sent customers:
```python
# batch example
inputs = [r.text for r in batch]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-xl", input=inputs)
# use response order mapping -> less calls, lower unit count
```
customer-ACME: deploying change now, I'll confirm after next run. very appreciative of the fast help :relieved:
raj (Billing): credit applied (20,000). please allow up to 1 hour to reflect in the console.
customer-ACME: saw the credit, thank you. also opened an issue to improve our monitoring for cost anomalies.
emma (Support): closing loop: we filed a docs task to highlight retry-patterns and batching best-practices; tagging eng and billing. reach out if anything else crops up :thumbsup:
